_about.purpose: Candidate queries to extend the Phase 11 evaluation set into the topics the corpus actually covers. Step 3 of the 6j plan, and the direct consequence of 6m: the existing 22 queries are almost entirely modern fungal leaf diseases, which the coverage check showed the classical texts cannot address (4 strong / 5 marginal / 13 none). Evaluating only on those measures the system against questions with no answer.
_about.method: Written from the DOMAIN, not from the corpus. Each query is something a farmer or gardener would plausibly ask, in the subject areas these treatises are known to cover (pest damage, soil preparation, seed treatment, sowing season, water, manure, planting, physical injury to trees, poor growth). Specific passages were NOT consulted while drafting, because choosing queries to match passages we had already read would make the evaluation circular - we would be testing retrieval on text selected for matching.
_about.honesty: These are CANDIDATES with no expect_answerable label. The label is assigned only after scripts/check_coverage.py scores each one with the pipeline's own cross-encoder, using the same thresholds as 6m: >=0.35 strong, 0.15-0.35 marginal, <0.15 none. Some are expected to fail, and those are kept as honest negatives rather than deleted.
_about.style: Symptom-led or task-led phrasing, matching the existing set and the output of the Strategy-B bridge. The crop is deliberately absent or incidental, because the texts are symptom-general (6d.1).
_about.grading: Each candidate was graded by READING its retrieved passages, not by its cross-encoder score. The score alone proved unsafe here: it marked 16/16 'strong' (up to 0.987) while several top-1 passages were plainly off-topic - n13 'how to plant a sapling' returned text about WHERE to cultivate vegetables (0.985), and n16 'protecting stored grain' returned a materials table about roots and branches (0.625). The score measures vocabulary overlap, so it is reliable evidence of ABSENCE (the 0.06 scores in 6m really do mean nothing matches) but not of PRESENCE. Grades are the author's reading and await expert ratification, like the rest of this silver set.

queries.query: small soft insects clustered on new shoots making the leaves curl
queries.rationale: aphid-type damage; sap-sucking pests are a major traditional concern
queries.grade_reason: NITI section_10 only IDENTIFIES aphid->curled leaves; no remedy in top-1

queries.query: caterpillars chewing holes through the leaves of a young plant
queries.rationale: biting and chewing damage, the most visible pest symptom
queries.grade_reason: top-1 is about raising plants from seed; top-2 only identifies the pest

queries.query: ants swarming around the roots and base of a tree
queries.rationale: ant infestation, a named concern in classical tree-care
queries.grade_reason: Table 1 lists ants with symptoms AND treatment; v.173-189 covers ant damage

queries.query: how to prepare a natural spray to keep insects away from crops
queries.rationale: preparation-style question rather than symptom-style; tests the recipe content
queries.grade_reason: top-1 is layering/propagation; the right section (6.2.8) is only at top-2

queries.query: treating seeds before sowing so that they germinate well and resist disease
queries.rationale: seed treatment is standard in these treatises
queries.grade_reason: top-1 and top-2 are both the Beejamrit seed-treatment recipe

queries.query: how to tell whether a piece of land is suitable for planting trees
queries.grade_reason: Kashyapiya land description + Vrik v.38-58 'land recommended for planting'

queries.query: enriching poor soil with manure before planting
queries.grade_reason: Kashyapiya: plough four or five times, then apply cow dung

queries.query: preparing a liquid manure from animal and plant materials to feed the roots
queries.rationale: kunapajala-type liquid manure; a well-documented practice
queries.grade_reason: top-1 off-topic; kunapa water appears only as a row in a materials table

queries.query: the proper season and month for sowing different kinds of crops
queries.rationale: seasonal agronomy, a core subject of Krishi Parashara
queries.grade_reason: NITI gives crop-specific banana/turmeric calendars, not general season guidance

queries.query: natural signs in the sky and in animals that indicate rain is coming
queries.rationale: rainfall prognostication, a core subject of Brihat Samhita
queries.grade_reason: Brihat ch.28: ants shifting eggs, snakes mating, chameleons gazing up

queries.query: how much and how often a young tree should be watered
queries.grade_reason: Vrik v.110-125 gives an exact schedule by soil type and season

queries.query: finding underground water before digging a well
queries.rationale: water divining; Brihat Samhita chapter 54 was ingested for this
queries.grade_reason: Kashyapiya covers WHEN to dig, not how to locate water; Brihat ch.54 not retrieved

queries.query: the right way to plant and transplant a sapling so it survives
queries.grade_reason: top-1 is WHERE to cultivate, not HOW to plant or transplant

queries.query: a tree branch broken by strong wind and how to treat the wound
queries.rationale: physical injury; the texts treat wounds explicitly
queries.grade_reason: Table 1: if branches fall off, dress the spot with honey and ghee

queries.query: a tree that does not flower or bear fruit even though it looks healthy
queries.grade_reason: Upavanavinoda 177: windy-humour trees 'do not bear flowers and fruits'

queries.query: protecting harvested grain from insects during storage
queries.rationale: post-harvest storage; included expecting it may fail, as a fair negative
queries.grade_reason: top-1 is a materials table about roots/branches; top-2 is threshing, not storage
